text:
maria: Heads up — we're designing the external-log-export path for security logs (syslog -> export-proxy -> external SIEM). Need input on retention segmentation, RBAC for consumer teams, and how we should handle KMS wrapping for exported data. TL;DR: regs want encryption in flight+at rest and an auditable key usage pattern.

sam: For KMS wrapping I'd lean envelope encryption: export-proxy encrypts with a data key, data key wrapped by a KMS key per-destination (or per-tenant if multi-tenant). That way we only grant unwrap rights to the proxy and the archive process. Avoid giving SIEM direct decrypt rights.

jess: Agree on envelope. On RBAC: propose 3 roles -> `log-viewer` (read-only within retained UI), `log-exporter` (write to export buckets/sockets), `incident-elevate` (just-in-time, time-limited elevation with MFA and approval). Audit every grant request.

li: Cost/ops note: retention tiers matter. High-sensitivity (auth, audit, infra changes) -> 90d hot, 365d cold; general app logs -> 30d hot, 365d archive. Put export-only copies in a separate S3 bucket with lifecycle + immutable retention if regs require.

ashok: SIEM vendor asks for TLS syslog + client cert auth. Can the proxy terminate TLS and sign to SIEM? I'd rather have the proxy do TLS to vendor and keep internal channel TLS+, decrypt only in the proxy, then re-encrypt with envelope before writing to bucket.

maria: Good. Two questions: 1) Should we use a single KMS key per vendor or per cluster? 2) How to handle emergency incident access where SRE needs short-term decryption?

sam: 1) Per-vendor key is simpler for audits (separate key MR per partner). Per-tenant gives stronger isolation but increases key sprawl and rotation complexity. Recommend per-vendor for first pass, add per-tenant later for high-risk customers.

jess: 2) For emergency access use short-lived grants: create a workflow where incident-elevate triggers a temporary KMS grant via an approval flow (PagerDuty+Okta). Log the grant, require justification, and auto-revoke after window. Example pseudo-policy: 
```
# example: incident-elevate flow
- requestor: SRE on-call
- approval: 2 members from sec-eng or manager
- duration: 1 hour
- audit: append justification to ticket
```

li: Also add query-level masking for exported data: drop PII fields before export unless the vendor contract allows it. That reduces regulator exposure.

ashok: For the proxy config, here's a quick snippet we'll test: 
```
forwarder:
  listen: 0.0.0.0:6514
  tls: true
  client_cert_required: true
  destination:
    tls: true
    endpoint: siem.example.com:6514
    cert: /etc/ssl/siem-client.pem
encryption:
  envelope: true
  kms_key_alias: alias/exports/siem-vendor-a
```

maria: Nice. For RBAC enforcement, can infra gate the `log-exporter` role to only the proxy EC2 instance profile and the export lambda? We should avoid human creds being able to write to export buckets directly.

sam: Yes — use instance-profile or service-principal based IAM roles bound to the proxy. Human accounts only get `log-viewer` and `incident-elevate` (JIT). Add resource-level policies on S3 that deny PutObject unless caller is the proxy role or the export lambda.

ashok: Will set up an S3 bucket policy like: `Condition: ArnEquals:aws:PrincipalARN: arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:role/export-proxy` and `kms:ViaService` checks for KMS wrap.

jess: Can we formalize this into an RFC? I'll draft RBAC + KMS grant playbook and a short runbook for incident-elevate. If folks agree I'll open a PR to infra-terraform.

maria: Please do. Also create a short audit checklist: who requested export, which key used, which objects were shipped, and retention class. That will help compliance reviews.

infra-bot: Ticket created: SEC-EXPORT-4127 -> "Export proxy RBAC + KMS playbook" assigned to @jess, due 7d. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-EXPORT-4127 :white_check_mark:

jess: I'll put the draft in the ticket and ping for review.

li: Quick follow-up — can we include a monthly job that verifies KMS grants and lists active grants for each export key? Add to runbook.

maria: Good call. Also add a weekly check that exported buckets have lifecycle rules intact and no public ACLs.

ashok: I'll prototype the proxy TLS cert rotation and show perf for 10k msgs/s.

sam: thumbs up — sounds like a plan. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks all — marking this resolved for now. We'll review RFC and ticket updates next week. :eyes:
